mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where this trigger is met, based on out-of-sample walk-forward testing.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met in at least 3 out of 5 historical episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between the trigger and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 4 out of 6 historical instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both CPIAUCSL (below 2%) and FEDFUNDS (below 1%) for two consecutive months signals a deflationary monetary easing regime, which historically has been associated with equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS < 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 3 out of 5 episodes where this joint trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between PAYEMS and UNRATE over three months (i.e., both rising) signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 4 out of 6 historical episodes when this interaction is present.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above 5% for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which historically boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 3 out of 5 historical episodes when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS growth) exceeding 3% for two consecutive quarters signals strengthening household purchasing power, which drives up demand and boosts corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 5 out of 8 historical quarters where this always-on condition is met.
